title: Unknown-word protocol
summary: Use structure, context and elimination to keep moving when a tested word is unfamiliar.

provenance.authored_by: Codex English V3-B Sprint breadth milestone

sections.title: Notice what remains knowable
content: An unfamiliar word does not make the sentence unknowable. Mark contrast, cause, examples and tone first.

sections.title: Use S-C-A-N
content: Structure: identify word class. Context: paraphrase the surrounding logic. Alternatives: eliminate options that break grammar or meaning. Next: commit, flag and move.

sections.title: Test a candidate meaning
content: In ‘The plan was viable because the team had enough time and materials’, because supplies a feasibility clue; viable must mean workable.

sections.title: Explain every elimination
content: For each option, state whether grammar, logic, tone or evidence removes it. Do not select by familiarity alone.

sections.title: Use a timed stop rule
content: After one structured scan, choose the best-supported option, flag uncertainty and continue. Return only if time remains.

sections.title: Diagnose the failed step
content: Record unknown meaning, missed clue, option trap or tone mismatch so the next practice targets the process.

sections.title: Transfer the protocol
content: Resolve five unfamiliar words in different contexts before viewing feedback.
